summary: Gu Rong Gyalsé Chökyi Lodrö was a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Gualtherus Hendrik Mees (1903–1955) worked in religious studies and Indology. He earned an M.A. from the University of Cambridge (~1925–1928) and an LL.D. from Leiden University (~1928–1935), studying under Jean Philippe Vogel.

Guang Xing is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of London (SOAS) under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy Hugh Barrett. He held posts at the University of Hong Kong and the University of British Columbia.

Guangchang Fang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He worked as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1986–2004) and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University around 2004.

Guankong (1903–1989) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught at the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies and served as a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China beginning in 1957.

Gudo Wafu Nishijima (1919–2014) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied law at the University of Tokyo and trained under Kodo Sawaki and Rempo Niwa. He lectured at the University of Tokyo and Eastern Institute, and founded Dogen Sangha International.

Gudrun Bühnemann is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bonn, Münster, and Vienna (PhD under Ernst Steinkellner), also studying under Michael Hahn. She held research posts in India and Japan before joining the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992.

Gudrun Melzer is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of Munich under Jens-Uwe Hartmann. As of 2026, she holds research posts at the University of Munich, the Göttingen Academy, and the IIBS.

Guilherme de Vasconcelos Abreu (1842–1907) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Coimbra and under Abel Bergaigne and Martin Haug. In 1877, he became Professor of Sanskrit at Curso Superior de Letras.

Guillaume Le Gentil (1725–1792) was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the Faculté de théologie catholique de Paris and the Collège de France. He held a post at the Paris Observatory from circa 1753 to 1792.

Guillaume Oisel is a linguist and Tibetologist who earned a doctorate in linguistics from Sorbonne Nouvelle University (2006–2013). In 2019, he served as a docente at the National University of San Marcos.
Gunapala Dharmasiri is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who held an academic post at the University of Peradeniya, attested in 1991 and 2008.
Gunilla Gren-Eklund is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied under Stig Wikander and Nils Simonsson, and held an academic post at Uppsala University from circa 1978 to 2003.

Gunnar Jarring (1907–2002) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his studies at Lund University (~1926–1933) and served on its faculty from circa 1933 to 1940.

Guo Jun is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney, training under Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin. He is attested as abbot of Mahabodhi Monastery in 2013.
Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Rissho University (~1997–2005) under Kenyu Mitomo. He also studied under Sheng Yen, Hoyo Watanabe, and several other teachers.
Gurii Stepanov (1880–1937) was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Kazan Theological Seminary and Kazan Theological Academy, where he was appointed Docent of Kalmuk in 1909.

Gurinder Singh Mann is a religious studies and Indology scholar with degrees from Kent, Harvard, and Columbia (Ph.D. ~1993). He taught at Columbia (1988–1999) and held the Kundan Kaur Kapany Chair at UC Santa Barbara (1999–2015).

id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga (1874–1957) was a religious studies scholar who earned a Dr.Theol. at Leiden University. He was Professor of New Testament and Comparative Religion at the University of Amsterdam and later Docent at Utrecht University.

Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Richard Burghart, also studying under Hla Pe and John Okell. He served as a Senior Teaching Fellow at SOAS.
